Rugged tablet for Procore

Procore is construction management software. Its support documentation covers a Procore app for Android with tools such as Drawings, Inspections, Photos, Purchase Orders and Subcontracts, alongside the web application used in an office. On site, the app is where drawings are read, photos are attached and inspection items are signed, which means a device used on scaffolds, in muddy groundworks and in site cabins, carried all day and often put down wet.

This page sets out what Procore publishes about the Android versions and Windows versions it supports, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, and which one does not. The important point is that Procore's Android app currently requires Android 13 or later, which rules out some devices that would run other field apps.

A UK construction or contracting business can buy a single unit to try before buying for the whole team.

Requirements

What Procore needs from a device

Each item below comes from Procore Technologies's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform: Android 13 or later, installed from Google Play

    Procore's Android requirements article says the Procore Android app currently requires Android 13 or later, and that earlier versions of Android stopped being supported in February 2026. A device on an older version can keep using an installed copy until one year after support was removed for that Android version. The article says the app should only be installed from Google Play and that Procore does not support issues arising from installations outside it. Source: support.procore.com

  • Memory, storage, screen size and processor: not published

    The Android requirements article gives no RAM, storage, screen-size or processor figure, and lists no supported device models. Procore does recommend using the most recent Android version available for your device. Source: support.procore.com

  • Offline: items viewed and cached earlier can be viewed or edited offline

    The Drawings permissions article for Android says many items can be viewed or edited in offline mode provided the item was previously viewed and cached on your mobile device. Some linking actions are marked as able to be performed offline, and the article says tasks performed offline are synced with Procore once a network connection has been reestablished. That means open the drawings and items you need while you have a connection, before you go to a site with poor signal. We found no published list of every tool that works offline. Source: support.procore.com

  • Photos: device camera, device library or the project Photos tool

    The Android guide to adding photos to a drawing lists three sources: Choose from Procore, which selects an existing photo from the project's Photos tool; Choose from Library, which selects a photo file from the device's photo library; and Camera, which takes a new photo with the device camera. The page does not state a file size or photo count limit. Source: support.procore.com

  • Signatures: drawn on the touchscreen when added as a signer

    In the Android app, a user who has been added as a signer opens the project's Inspections tool, taps the inspection, taps the signature icon beside their name in the Signatures section, draws the signature and submits it. The article does not mention offline signing, so do not assume it works without a connection. Source: support.procore.com

  • Windows: Procore Drive needs Windows 10 or newer, no hardware specification published

    Procore's setup guide for Procore Drive, its desktop file tool, says it can only be installed on a system running Microsoft Windows 10 or newer. The page lists no processor, memory or storage requirement. We did not fetch a Procore article listing supported web browsers, so this page makes no claim about which browsers Procore supports, and no native Windows version of the field app is documented in the pages we checked. Source: v2.support.procore.com

Setting up

Getting Procore running

  1. Ask your Procore account administrator to add the user to the project, with the permission level needed for the tools they will use, and as a signer on any inspection they will sign.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, open Google Play and install the Procore app (package com.procore.activities, developer Procore Technologies). Procore says the app should only be installed from Google Play.
  3. Check the Android version under Settings, About tablet. It should be Android 13 or later, which the A10 (Android 14) and A6 (Android 15) are.
  4. Fit a data SIM. Before going to a site with weak signal, open the drawings and items you will need so they are cached on the device.
  5. Accept the device prompts for the camera and photo library so photos can be taken or chosen from the library.
  6. On a Tuga W10 in the office, install Procore Drive if you use it, which needs Windows 10 or newer.
  7. For the A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.
